query: What operational burdens appear in incident descriptions?

per_column.name: operational_burden_type
per_column.rationale: This is a multi-label categorization of the burden itself (connectivity/infrastructure/software/outage/performance), which restates the whole concept as a typology rather than isolating a single non-overlapping aspect OF it. The overlapping pipe-delimited multi-values also show it is not carving out a distinct MECE facet but re-labeling the whole.

per_column.name: severity_indicator
per_column.rationale: Severity is a genuine aspect of an operational burden -- how heavy/impactful the burden is is a constitutive dimension (magnitude/intensity) of the burden concept.

per_column.name: root_infrastructure
per_column.rationale: The underlying/root infrastructure component (Network, Database, Software, Hardware) identifies the source or origin of the burden, i.e. what causes it, not a constitutive part of the burden itself.

judge.rationale: Only one of the three added columns (severity_indicator) qualifies as a constitutive facet capturing the magnitude/intensity dimension of operational burden. operational_burden_type is a restatement/typology of the whole concept (and its overlapping multi-label values undermine mutual exclusivity), while root_infrastructure identifies the causal source rather than an aspect of the burden. The type column heavily overlaps in meaning with the concept and with root_infrastructure (e.g. 'software'/'infrastructure' categories vs. Software/Hardware sources), lowering mutual exclusivity. As a facet set, exhaustiveness is poor: dimensions such as effort/labor cost, duration, breadth of impact, and recurrence are not covered, leaving the burden concept only partially decomposed.
